drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We propose an annual base salary of USD 400,000, subject to client approval, with participation in the company’s executive benefit plans. We have included twelve months’ salary continuation and continued health benefits for termination without Cause or resignation for Good Reason, together with narrow definitions and notice and cure protections. We have also deleted the post-employment non-compete and substituted confidentiality and trade-secret protections. Please see the revised provisions below.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. Subject to client approval of this proposal, the Executive shall receive an annual base salary of USD 400,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the health, retirement, paid leave, and other employee benefit plans made available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to applicable plan terms.
edits.name: Compensation and benefits

edits.text: 3. TERMINATION AND SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall provide twelve months of base salary continuation at the rate in effect immediately before termination or, if higher, before the reduction giving rise to Good Reason. During that period, the Company shall also continue the Executive’s and eligible dependents’ health coverage on the same contribution terms as apply to active senior executives, subject to applicable law and plan terms; if such continuation is unavailable, the Company shall provide a lawful economically equivalent benefit. Severance is in addition to accrued salary, reimbursable expenses, and vested benefits. “Cause” means the Executive’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty materially related to the Executive’s duties; willful fraud or embezzlement against the Company; or a willful and material breach of this Agreement that materially harms the Company. Cause excludes good-faith business judgment, ordinary negligence, and failure to achieve performance targets. Before terminating for Cause, the Company shall provide written notice specifying the grounds and at least thirty days to cure any curable conduct, together with a reasonable opportunity to respond to the Board. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in base salary, a material diminution in authority, duties, or responsibilities, relocation of the principal work location by more than fifty miles, or the Company’s material breach of this Agreement. The Executive must give written notice within ninety days after learning of the condition, allow thirty days for cure, and resign within sixty days after expiration of that cure period if the condition remains uncured. Payments and benefits shall be administered in compliance with applicable law, including Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code where applicable.
edits.name: Severance, Cause, and Good Reason

edits.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY AND TRADE SECRETS; NO POST-EMPLOYMENT NON-COMPETE. No post-employment non-compete restriction shall apply. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s nonpublic confidential business information except in performing duties for the Company or as authorized or required by law. This obligation excludes information that becomes public without breach, is lawfully obtained from another source without a duty of confidentiality, or is independently developed without use of Company confidential information. Trade secrets shall remain protected for so long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law; other confidential information shall be protected for two years after employment ends. Nothing restricts use of general skills and experience, lawful competition, protected reporting to government agencies, communications with counsel, or disclosures protected by whistleblower law. Under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), the Executive shall not be liable under federal or state trade-secret law for confidential disclosures to a government official or attorney solely to report or investigate a suspected legal violation, or for disclosures in a complaint or other document filed under seal. In a retaliation action, the Executive may disclose trade secrets to counsel and use them in the proceeding if filed under seal and not otherwise disclosed except by court order.
edits.name: Replace non-compete with confidentiality protections
